title: PV Sindhu Turns to Sports Science Ahead of BWF World Championships in Delhi
excerpt: The two-time Olympic medallist is leveraging strength and conditioning work in her bid for a record sixth World Championships medal, with the tournament starting August 17 at the Indira Gandhi Stadium.
body:
• PV Sindhu has intensified her sports science and strength and conditioning regimen ahead of the BWF World Championships 2026 in New Delhi, starting August 17.
  • Sindhu, seeded ninth in women's singles, is chasing a record sixth World Championships medal on home soil at the Indira Gandhi Stadium.
  • Coach Pullela Gopichand has called Sindhu a genuine contender, citing her uninterrupted fitness run this season as a key difference-maker.
  • India fields a 10-member squad including men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, seeded fifth.

Sindhu's Science-Driven Preparation

PV Sindhu is taking a methodical, science-driven approach to what could be the defining tournament of her 2026 season. The two-time Olympic medallist has invested heavily in sports science, strength and conditioning in the lead-up to the BWF World Championships, which begin on Sunday at New Delhi's Indira Gandhi Stadium.

The 31-year-old, who already holds five World Championships medals — one gold, two silver, and two bronze — is targeting an unprecedented sixth medal on home soil. No woman has achieved that mark in badminton singles.

Gopichand Backs Sindhu

Chief national coach Pullela Gopichand, in an exclusive interview with MyKhel, described Sindhu as a genuine contender for the title. He identified her fitness as the biggest change this season.

"The biggest difference this season has been Sindhu's fitness. After spending the previous two to three years battling recurring injuries, she has finally enjoyed an uninterrupted run on the circuit."

— Pullela Gopichand, Chief National Coach

Gopichand noted that apart from An Se-young of South Korea, he sees no unbeatable opponent in women's singles. "Everybody else is beatable," he said, adding that many top players still struggle to read Sindhu's unique style of play.

Home Advantage

The World Championships return to India after 17 years, and the home crowd factor looms large. Sindhu herself acknowledged the significance during the India Open earlier this year, held at the same venue. "It feels special when you're playing at your home ground," she said.

Her father PV Ramana, in an interview with RevSportz, expressed confidence in her preparation. "She is really working hard, and I am watching her closely. That shows she is in good shape. I hope she continues like this and gives her best performance," he said.

India's Full Squad

India's 10-member contingent includes several medal hopefuls. The men's doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, seeded fifth, are expected to challenge strongly — provided Satwik has fully recovered from a shoulder issue. Men's singles player Lakshya Sen received the 14th seeding, while the mixed doubles pair of Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto are seeded 15th.

The week-long tournament runs from August 17 to 23, with finals across all five disciplines scheduled for the closing day.

What to Watch

Sindhu's draw will be crucial. Her seeding at ninth means she could face top-ranked opponents as early as the quarterfinals. But with her fitness at peak levels and the Indira Gandhi Stadium crowd behind her, the stage is set for a memorable run in what she has called one of the most important tournaments of her career.
nri_angle: PV Sindhu, one of India's most celebrated athletes globally, chases a record sixth World Championships medal on home soil with the diaspora following closely.
